1.content:
## 1 - Did protection succeed, and what is at risk?

The daily operational question for a data-protection platform. `cohesity.protectiongroup.run.outcome` is a **delta counter** of runs reaching a terminal status, so it is summed over the timeframe, never averaged. `cohesity.protectiongroup.last_success.age` is the only signal for a job that never ran - a group missing from these tiles is silent, and silence is not success.

2.title: Protection run outcomes over time
2.description: Delta counter of runs reaching a terminal status, summed per interval and split by status. Runs that arrive without a status dimension are labelled Unknown rather than charted as an unnamed series.
2.query:
timeseries runs = sum(cohesity.protectiongroup.run.outcome), by:{status}
| fieldsAdd status = coalesce(status, "Unknown")

3.title: Run outcomes in this timeframe
3.description: Summed, not averaged - this is a delta counter. An empty tile means no run finished in the timeframe, which is not the same as every run succeeding. An Unknown slice is a run the cluster reported with no terminal status attached, not a run that failed.
3.query:
timeseries runs = sum(cohesity.protectiongroup.run.outcome, scalar:true), by:{status}
| filter runs > 0
| fields Outcome = coalesce(status, "Unknown"), Runs = runs
| sort Runs desc

4.title: Protection groups in SLA violation
4.description: Distinct protection groups whose cohesity.protectiongroup.sla_violated dimension is true.

5.title: Longest time since a successful run
5.description: Worst last_success.age across all protection groups, shown as a duration rather than raw milliseconds.
5.query:
timeseries age = max(cohesity.protectiongroup.last_success.age, scalar:true), by:{cohesity.protectiongroup.name}
| summarize `Longest time since a successful run` = duration(toLong(max(age)), unit:"ms")

singleValue.recordField: Longest time since a successful run
singleValue.label: Worst backup age

6.title: Time since last success, worst first
6.description: One row per protection group. Paused explains a deliberate silence; a group that has never succeeded simply has the largest age. Never read a 0 here as an alert condition.
6.query:
timeseries age = max(cohesity.protectiongroup.last_success.age, scalar:true), by:{cohesity.protectiongroup.name, cohesity.protectiongroup.sla_violated, cohesity.protectiongroup.paused, cohesity.protectiongroup.active}
| fieldsAdd `Time since last success` = duration(toLong(age), unit:"ms")
| fields `Protection group` = cohesity.protectiongroup.name, `Time since last success`, `SLA violated` = cohesity.protectiongroup.sla_violated, Paused = cohesity.protectiongroup.paused, Active = cohesity.protectiongroup.active
| sort `Time since last success` desc

7.title: Backup age distribution
7.description: How many protection groups sit in each staleness band.

10.content:
## 2 - Is capacity running out?

The slower burn that nobody looks at until it is urgent. Used percentage is **computed here from `capacity.used` and `capacity.total`** - the extension deliberately ingests no `used_pct` metric, because a stored derivative drifts from its inputs the moment one poll succeeds and the other fails. Resiliency overhead is not free space either: it is capacity the cluster holds for erasure coding or replication and will never hand back. Garbage bytes belong in this picture too, but this cluster is not serving them - see section 5.

11.title: Total capacity
11.query:
timeseries total = avg(cohesity.cluster.capacity.total)
| fields `Total capacity` = arrayLast(total)

12.title: Used capacity
12.query:
timeseries used = avg(cohesity.cluster.capacity.used)
| fields `Used capacity` = arrayLast(used)

13.title: Available capacity
13.query:
timeseries available = avg(cohesity.cluster.capacity.available)
| fields `Available capacity` = arrayLast(available)

14.title: Used %
14.description: Computed in DQL from capacity.used / capacity.total - there is no ingested used_pct metric on purpose.

15.title: Data reduction ratio
15.description: Logical bytes stored divided by physical bytes stored. The number capacity planning turns on.

21.title: Resiliency overhead
21.description: Bytes consumed cluster-wide by erasure coding or replication, summed across storage domains. Capacity the cluster holds and will never hand back, so capacity planning must not count it as free.

17.title: Cluster capacity over time
17.query: timeseries { Total = avg(cohesity.cluster.capacity.total), Used = avg(cohesity.cluster.capacity.used), Available = avg(cohesity.cluster.capacity.available) }, by:{cohesity.cluster.name}

18.title: Used % over time
18.description: The runway. Same DQL-side computation as the gauge, kept per interval.

19.title: Storage domains by usage
19.description: Logical, physical and resiliency overhead per storage domain. The three metrics are appended rather than fetched together so a domain still lists when one of them is absent - a missing number is left null, never rendered as 0.

20.title: Logical vs physical usage by service
20.description: Split by the service dimension - dataprotect or fileservices. The gap between the two lines is what deduplication and compression are buying.
20.query: timeseries { Logical = sum(cohesity.cluster.usage.logical), Physical = sum(cohesity.cluster.usage.physical) }, by:{service}

30.content:
## 3 - Where is the data actually moving?

Per-view read and write throughput, from the cluster's top-views ranking. **Expect gaps.** The endpoint behind this metric answers intermittently - it went silent for days and recovered on its own - so a bar appears only for the intervals the cluster answered. A gap here is the cluster declining to rank, not the view going idle, and not the extension failing: section 4 is what tells you that.

CPU, memory and I/O used to sit in this section. They come from a different cluster endpoint that is currently down, so they have moved to section 5.

35.title: View throughput over time
35.description: Summed across the ranked views and split by direction. Sparse by design - see the section note.

31.title: CPU and memory
31.query: timeseries { CPU = avg(cohesity.cluster.cpu.usage), Memory = avg(cohesity.cluster.memory.usage) }, by:{cohesity.cluster.name}

33.title: I/O latency by operation
33.description: Microseconds. Not converted to milliseconds - sub-millisecond is the signal on flash. From /stats/time-series-stats - see the section note.

34.title: Top views by throughput
34.description: View is a dimension, not an entity - the poll returns a top-N ranking, and rankings make bad entities.
34.query:
timeseries throughput = avg(cohesity.cluster.view.throughput, scalar:true), by:{cohesity.view.name, operation}
| filter isNotNull(throughput)
| fields View = cohesity.view.name, Operation = operation, Throughput = throughput
| sort Throughput desc
| limit 20

40.content:
## 4 - Is the extension actually collecting?

Every tile above goes blank both when Cohesity is broken and when the extension is broken. `cohesity.cluster.collection_success` is the only thing that tells those two apart. **Read the absence of a 1, never the presence of a 0** - a pre-identity failure reports under the configured cluster name rather than the discovered one, so the failure lands on a different series from the success.

41.title: Polls answered
41.query:
timeseries success = avg(cohesity.cluster.collection_success)
| fields `Polls answered` = arrayAvg(success) * 100.0

42.title: Collection success over time
42.description: A gap here is the extension going quiet. That is a different failure from a 0, and the two must not be conflated.

50.content:
## 5 - Metrics this cluster is not serving

The four tiles below are wired correctly and are blank for a reason outside Dynatrace. CPU, memory, IOPS, latency and garbage bytes all come from the cluster's `/stats/time-series-stats` endpoint, and on this cluster that endpoint answers **HTTP 500** - for every `entityId` shape the extension knows how to ask with. Nothing is being dropped on the way in: section 4 shows collection succeeding throughout.

They are kept rather than deleted because this failure is **intermittent, not permanent**. The `/stats/top-views` endpoint behind section 3 failed exactly the same way for days and recovered with no intervention. These tiles need no redeploy to come back - the moment the cluster answers, they fill in.

If they are still blank, the thing to investigate is the Cohesity cluster, not the extension.

16.title: Garbage awaiting collection
16.description: Bytes held by data pending garbage collection. Capacity planning must not count these as free. From /stats/time-series-stats - see the section note.
16.query:
timeseries garbage = avg(cohesity.cluster.garbage.bytes)
| fields `Garbage awaiting collection` = arrayLast(garbage)

60.content:
## 6 - Cluster alerts

Cohesity's own health events, ingested as log records under `cohesity_storage.alerts`. These describe the **cluster**, not the data it protects: no usernames, no source addresses and no backup content.

**These tiles are blank unless alerts are switched on.** They are off by default - *Collect cluster alerts as logs* on the monitoring configuration. A blank tile here means the collection is off, not that the cluster is healthy.

Counts are of **distinct alerts**, not records: an alert that fires, resolves and fires again is two occurrences of one alert, and counting records would make a flapping alert look like an outbreak. `kNote` is Cohesity's informational state, not a problem.

61.title: Open critical alerts
61.description: Distinct alerts at critical severity still in the kOpen state. The number to look at first.
61.query:
fetch logs
| filter log.source == "cohesity_storage.alerts"
| filter cohesity.alert.severity == "critical"
| filter cohesity.alert.state == "kOpen"
| summarize `Open critical` = countDistinctExact(cohesity.alert.id)

62.title: Open warning alerts
62.description: Distinct alerts at warning severity still in the kOpen state.
62.query:
fetch logs
| filter log.source == "cohesity_storage.alerts"
| filter cohesity.alert.severity == "warning"
| filter cohesity.alert.state == "kOpen"
| summarize `Open warning` = countDistinctExact(cohesity.alert.id)

63.title: Distinct alerts in this timeframe
63.description: Every severity and state. Compare with the two tiles to its left: a large number here against few open ones means the cluster raised and resolved a lot without anything being left outstanding.
63.query:
fetch logs
| filter log.source == "cohesity_storage.alerts"
| summarize `Alerts` = countDistinctExact(cohesity.alert.id)

64.title: Unreadable severities
64.description: Alerts whose severity this extension could not map. Normally zero. A non-zero value is not a cluster problem - it means Cohesity used a severity name the extension does not know, it is being reported at WARN to be safe, and domain._ALERT_SEVERITIES needs the new name. The diagnostics channel names it.
64.query:
fetch logs
| filter log.source == "cohesity_storage.alerts"
| filter cohesity.alert.severity == "unknown"
| summarize `Unmapped` = countDistinctExact(cohesity.alert.id)

65.title: Alerts raised over time, by severity
65.description: When the cluster started complaining. Records, not distinct alerts: here the repeats are the signal, because a spike is what a degrading cluster looks like.

66.title: What is complaining
66.description: Distinct alerts by category and severity. kBackupRestore dominating is normal on a busy protection estate; kNodeHealth or kDataPath appearing is not.
66.query:
fetch logs
| filter log.source == "cohesity_storage.alerts"
| summarize `Alerts` = countDistinctExact(cohesity.alert.id), by:{`Category` = cohesity.alert.category, `Severity` = cohesity.alert.severity}
| sort `Alerts` desc

67.title: Most recent alerts
67.description: The newest occurrence of each alert, with the sentence the cluster wrote. The description can be withheld per cluster - Include alert descriptions - in which case this column is empty and every other one still works.
67.query:
fetch logs
| filter log.source == "cohesity_storage.alerts"
| fields `Time` = timestamp, `Severity` = cohesity.alert.severity, `Alert` = cohesity.alert.name, `Category` = cohesity.alert.category, `State` = cohesity.alert.state, `Detail` = cohesity.alert.description
| sort `Time` desc
| limit 100
